title: Implication for count-sort states
statement: Let $\mu$ be an initial memory, $A$ counting-sort arguments, $e\in\mathbb{Z}$, $R,R'$ predicates on integer-valued memories, and $\sigma$ a state. If $\sigma$ can be represented using entry value $e$ and a memory $\mu'$ that agrees with $\mu$ outside the destination and scratch regions and satisfies $R$, and every memory satisfying $R$ also satisfies $R'$, then $\sigma$ has such a representation with a memory satisfying $R'$.
hypotheses_covered: $\sigma$ satisfies the count-sort state predicate at entry $e$ with property $R$
replaced:
Let a state be represented by a location function and a memory function, and let $A$
specify the count-sort array and scratch-cell layout. If the state has entry value $e$,
some associated integer parameters, and a memory that agrees with the initial memory
outside the destination and counter ranges and satisfies a property $R$, and if every
memory satisfying $R$ also satisfies $R'$, then the same state has entry value $e$,
agrees with the initial memory outside those ranges, and satisfies $R'$.
